enrollment.machinesUsingThisToken: Machines using this token connect immediately, without approval.

enrollment.name: Name
enrollment.bulkHint: One token for a batch of machines. A device is created on its first connection — there is no need to add it in advance.
enrollment.groupHint: Everything connecting with this token lands in the group — no need to assign it to each machine by hand.
enrollment.approvalHint: Devices go into the queue: they connect and report inventory, but do not run scripts until approved. Clear the checkbox only when the token is going into a closed network.
enrollment.saveNow: Save the command now — the token cannot be looked up again.
enrollment.listFailed: Failed to load the list — the queue may NOT be empty.
enrollment.queueEmpty: The queue is empty — new devices appear here as soon as they connect with a bulk token. The list refreshes itself.
enrollment.notConnectedHint: The device was created, but the agent has never made contact. Older than a day usually means leftovers from an interrupted installation: the token is already dead and the machine is not coming.
enrollment.deleteWarn: “{{name}}” has never made contact, so deleting it only affects the record in the panel — nothing happens on the machine itself. If an agent is installed there after all, it will create the device again.
enrollment.tokenStorageHint: The token itself is not stored — only its fingerprint. Leaked or no longer needed — revoke it.
enrollment.noTokens: No bulk tokens — “Issue a token” onboards a batch of machines with a single command.
enrollment.revokeWarn: Machines that have not connected with it yet will not be able to enroll — the installation command has to be reissued with a new token. Devices already onboarded stay in the fleet: revoking does not take them out of service.
enrollment.revokeUses: This token has already been used {{count}} time(s).
enrollment.rejectWarn: “{{name}}” loses access: the status is terminal and cannot be reversed by approval — the machine has to be enrolled again.
enrollment.approveAllWarn: Currently in the queue: {{count}}. Approval lifts the restriction and gives the machines full access, including running scripts. It applies to everyone in the queue at the moment of confirmation — including those that may have connected while you were reading the list.
enrollment.rejectAllWarn: Devices to be rejected: {{count}}. The status is terminal — they can only be brought back by enrolling again.
enrollment.intuneHint: Copy this script and add it to your current MDM (for example, to Microsoft Intune as a PowerShell Script or a Win32 App). It downloads and installs the RoutineOps agent automatically. After the migration you can remove the old MDM profile.
enrollment.jamfHint: Copy this script and add it to your current MDM (for example, Jamf or Workspace ONE). It downloads the .pkg and performs the enrollment automatically. After the migration the old MDM profile can be removed.

deviceDetail.cannotDeleteRecoveryKeys: Cannot delete: recovery keys are in escrow

deviceDetail.escrowHint1: The server keeps them encrypted only and cannot decrypt them.
deviceDetail.blindTitle: Reports, lock statuses and security events from the device are not arriving
deviceDetail.escrowHint2: The downloaded file is opened offline with the <0>routineops-unseal</0> utility and the private key shares.
deviceDetail.uninstallHint: The agent does not run a command you send: it takes a fresh inventory snapshot, finds this entry on its own side and uses its own removal method. If the program was updated or its key changed in the meantime, the removal does not happen — you see “target changed” rather than a version removed by mistake.
deviceDetail.deleteWarn: “{{name}}” and its whole history (tasks, scripts, alerts, group membership) will be deleted irreversibly. If the agent is still alive, the device reappears on its next connection — decommission it first.
deviceDetail.moveHint: Group membership is cleared: groups belong to the current tenant, and a device left in them would fall under someone else's policies. The certificate is not reissued — it identifies the machine, not the department.
deviceDetail.decommissionHint: The agent removes itself from “{{name}}”: the service, the certificate, the private key, data directories and its own binary. This cannot be undone — bringing the machine back under management means enrolling it again.
deviceDetail.decommissionDelivery: The command is delivered once the device makes contact. The status changes to “Decommissioned” only after the agent confirms it; if the machine never comes back online, remove the agent by hand. This is not a kill switch: stolen hardware needs an access block.
deviceDetail.revealSaved: The file is saved. It is encrypted — decrypt it offline, on a machine holding the escrow private key shares:
deviceDetail.revealAudited: The reveal is recorded in the audit log. Do not keep the decrypted secret in chats or tickets.
deviceDetail.rebootDelayHint: The delay is the time an employee has to save their work. Once it passes, applications are closed by force, and a scheduled reboot cannot be cancelled from the panel.
deviceDetail.rebootNoWarningHint: On macOS and Linux an employee in a graphical session will not see the warning — tell them yourself.
